keywords: how to look up a data type
title: DataType is a stable information ID
summary: A DataType is a stable information ID with a shape. Look it up with find_history_data or get_dtype_map, then pick an entry by shape.
narrative:
A DataType is a stable information ID plus a consumption shape. It is not a table column name and not a downloader. You write a string such as close, close|b, or close_E_d. You do not construct DataType(...) for everyday work.

Two string forms:
- Wide name: close, pe, close|b. The framework matches frequency and asset type; if several candidates remain, it errors instead of guessing.
- Full id: close_E_d. The rightmost segments are frequency and asset type; the rest is the wide name. Prefer full ids in strategies when names collide.

Three symbol families (do not mix them):
- Pipe for adjustment: close|b (backward), close|f (forward).
- Hyphen to pull one symbol into a reference series: close-000300.SH.
- Underscore for a full id: close_E_d.

Find types with qt.find_history_data('pe') or a Chinese keyword, or browse datatypes.get_dtype_map(). The full catalog has a thousand rows; do not memorize it. After a hit, read the shape first, then choose an entry. Empty results are often a wrong shape or a local table that was never downloaded for that date window — check the entry, the starter tables, and overview.

This card does not teach filtering steps. Filtering is a separate question.
python_code:
import qteasy as qt
print(qt.find_history_data('pe'))
from qteasy import datatypes
print(len(datatypes.get_dtype_map()))
risk_notes: A catalog hit does not mean every id can go through get_history_data. Check shape and usable_in first.
